data.standardized_narrative: The 2020 calendar year resulted in a loss for Syndicate 2987, driven by an underwriting loss and a combined ratio of 113.9%. Gross premiums written increased by 3.1%, primarily in core Direct classes (Specialty, Property, Cyber) and Reinsurance (Property Treaty), benefiting from positive rating movements and market opportunities, partially offset by reduced demand in A&H, Contingency, and Political and Credit Risks due to COVID-19. The syndicate experienced significant uncertainty due to COVID-19, increased frequency and severity of major and medium loss events (attributed to climate change, population growth, and increasing insured values), and pressures on attritional ratios from soft market years (2017-2018) and social inflation in US Casualty. Political and economic volatility, falling yields, and trade tensions also contributed to a challenging environment. Despite these challenges, the syndicate noted improving attritional claims ratios, rate increases, and withdrawal of capacity in certain classes as causes for optimism. No specific gross prior year reserve development figure was explicitly stated or reliably derivable due to potential distortions from a Reinsurance to Close transaction.
raw_causal_phrases: continued positive rating movements building on that of 2019 and 2018
capitalising on market opportunities as they arose
targeted growth within business initiatives such as Scion
reduced demand in A&H, Contingency and Political and Credit Risks classes, due to the impact of COVID-19 related restrictions

significant fall in yields, as the Federal Reserve delivered two emergency interest rate cuts totalling 150bps in response to the emerging economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, boosted unrealised gains from fixed income securities
Realised losses were recorded on the equity portfolio following market sell-offs in the first quarter of 2020

The frequency of major events and the magnitude of the resulting claims continues to rise, with 2020's experience following on from those of 2017 and 2018, the most costly back-to-back years on record

The impact of medium loss events is also uncertain, with commentators attributing an increase in the frequency and severity of such events to climate change and other factors such as population growth and increasing insured values
pressures on attritional ratios continue, largely driven by the soft market years of 2017 and 2018 and by social inflation in the US Casualty market

Political and economic uncertainty and challenges continue. 2020 saw continued volatility in financial markets and experienced weakening growth, recession fears, falling yields, heightened tension around international trade and loose monetary policy
rate increases, the withdrawal of capacity in the market from certain classes and the Syndicate's improving attritional claims ratio
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross prior year development figure was found. The claims development triangle is potentially distorted by a Reinsurance to Close (RITC) transaction mentioned on page 12/13, which states it had no economic impact but could affect the appearance of reserve movements in the triangle. Therefore, prior year development could not be reliably extracted.
